opportunities.title: Unified context assembly pipeline with provenance and token budgeting
opportunities.detail: Replace the ad-hoc string concatenation in latticeai/api/chat.py:365-418 (LANGUAGE hint + vault + KG + OCR + files + recent chat appended in fixed order, no size control) with a ContextAssembler service: each candidate context item (workspace memory, KG node, conversation snippet, file) carries source id, retrieval score, and provenance; assembler dedupes, ranks across tiers, enforces a token budget per model, and emits the assembled context plus a machine-readable provenance manifest. The existing build_graph_trace/record_trace plumbing already streams trace_id to the client, so the manifest has a natural home — extend the trace to cover ALL injected context, not just KG matches.

opportunities.title: Wire hybrid/vector search into the chat inference path
opportunities.detail: SearchService.hybrid_search (latticeai/services/search_service.py, weights text/graph/vector) and KnowledgeGraph.vector_search already exist and are tested, but chat uses only LIKE-based context_for_query. Swap the chat retrieval call to the hybrid engine (and use it inside MemoryService.recall), so the vector index actually participates in inference-time memory. Small seam change, big retrieval-quality payoff once a real embedding provider is configured.

opportunities.title: Automatic episodic-to-semantic memory consolidation
opportunities.detail: Today MEMORY_KINDS records (preferences/decisions/working_style/long_term) are only written via manual POST /workspace/memories — nothing learns from conversations. Build a consolidation job (reusing the agent memory_update LLM-extraction pattern in latticeai/core/agent.py:417 but writing structured upsert_memory records instead of markdown dumps) that mines chat/agent runs for durable facts, preferences, and decisions, links each memory to its source Message/AIResponse KG nodes for provenance, and promotes short_term → long_term over time. This is the core 'Digital Brain learns about you' capability that is entirely missing.

opportunities.title: Durable conversation store to replace the 50-message chat_history.json
opportunities.detail: Move conversation history to SQLite (or read it back from the KG Message/AIResponse nodes that are already durably ingested via ingest_message). Keep chat_history.json only as a render cache if needed. This makes the 'conversation' memory tier real, makes /history/search useful beyond the last 50 messages, and lets build_recent_chat_context retrieve per-conversation windows correctly. Include user/conversation scoping to fix the cross-user assistant-message leak.

opportunities.title: Inject workspace memories into chat and agent prompts
opportunities.detail: Add a step in the chat context build (and AgentDeps in latticeai/core/agent.py) that recalls top-k relevant MEMORY_KINDS records (preferences, decisions, working_style) for the current user and injects them as a '[USER MEMORY]' block. The storage, search, and API already exist (workspace_os.search_memories); only the inference-time consumer is missing. This is the cheapest possible win toward the Digital Brain promise.

opportunities.title: Structured experience and decision records from agent runs
opportunities.detail: record_agent_run already persists plan, timeline, review_history, retry_history (latticeai/core/workspace_os.py:1290). Promote these into first-class KG node types (Experience, Decision, Outcome) via the v3.6.0 IngestionPipeline so future planning can retrieve 'what happened last time we tried X' with provenance. Replace the fire-and-forget memory_update markdown dump and the simulated multi_agent researcher snapshots with these real records.

opportunities.title: Merge the p_reinforce markdown vault into the Knowledge Graph
opportunities.detail: The brain vault (~/.ltcai-brain) and the KG are two disconnected knowledge stores with two different retrieval paths injected into the same prompt. Ingest vault files through services/ingestion.py (it already handles files with provenance) so the vault becomes Obsidian-compatible *storage/export* while retrieval converges on one indexed surface. Delete get_relevant_context's per-message full-vault rglob scan.

opportunities.title: Honest, unified relevance scoring in recall
opportunities.detail: Fix the matches/results key bug, then replace hardcoded scores (0.6 workspace, 0.5 graph fallback) with real normalized scores: vector cosine where embeddings exist, BM25-ish lexical score otherwise, with the score's method recorded per result ('vector'|'lexical'|'recency'). Same for build_graph_trace confidence — either compute it from retrieval scores or rename it to 'coverage' so the UI doesn't present an invented number as confidence.

opportunities.title: Memory lifecycle management (decay, promotion, conflict resolution)
opportunities.detail: Extend MemoryService beyond prune/compact-exact-dup: TTL/decay for short_term, promotion rules to long_term, contradiction detection between memories (e.g., changed preferences), and raising the silent caps (memories[-500:], traces[-200:], snapshots[-200:]) into configurable retention policies with archival export via the existing kg_portability backup path instead of silent deletion.

problems.title: Workspace 'personal memory' tier is never consumed at inference time
problems.detail: MEMORY_KINDS memories (preferences, decisions, working_style, long_term...) stored in workspace_os.json are only written manually via POST /workspace/memories (latticeai/api/workspace.py:405-419) and are never injected into chat or agent model context. The chat path (latticeai/api/chat.py:365-418) injects vault + KG + recent history but never calls search_memories/recall. The only inference-adjacent consumer is platform_runtime._context_provider (latticeai/services/platform_runtime.py:107-114), which feeds the simulated multi_agent role runner, not a real LLM. For a 'Digital Brain', the flagship personal-memory tier is effectively a UI-only display feature.

problems.title: MemoryService.recall graph branch is dead code (wrong response key)
problems.detail: memory_service.py:224 calls `self._kg.search(q, limit).get("results", [])` but KnowledgeGraph.search returns `{"query":..., "matches": [...]}` (knowledge_graph.py:3785-3797). The graph portion of /api/memory/recall therefore always returns zero results, silently (the except swallows nothing because no exception occurs). The unit test masks this by constructing the service with knowledge_graph=None, enable_graph=False (tests/unit/test_v32_platform.py:123), so 455 passing tests prove nothing about graph recall.

problems.title: Conversation memory is capped at 50 messages globally and silently truncated
problems.detail: save_to_history (latticeai/server_app.py:659-668) hard-caps chat_history.json at the last 50 messages across ALL users, conversations, and sources. Everything the Memory Manager reports as the 'conversation' tier, /history/search, and build_recent_chat_context operates on this 50-message window. Older episodic history survives only as KG Message/AIResponse nodes (retrievable solely via LIKE search). A platform whose pitch is 'knowledge is durable' silently deletes its primary conversation record; the Memory UI tier counts are therefore misleading.

problems.title: Fabricated relevance scores and synthesized 'confidence' presented as real
problems.detail: MemoryService.recall hardcodes score=0.6 for every workspace memory and defaults 0.5 for graph hits (memory_service.py:218,234), then sorts by these constants — the ranking is fake. build_graph_trace 'confidence' (workspace_os.py:861-864) is an invented formula (0.35 + match_count ratio * 0.45 + 0.10 if edges), not a measured retrieval confidence; it is recorded into every answer trace and streamed to the client as if meaningful. This conflicts with the project's own 'nothing is fabricated' doctrine stated in memory_service.py's docstring.

problems.title: Chat inference never uses the vector/hybrid search engine; retrieval is SQLite LIKE substring matching
problems.detail: The chat path uses KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH.context_for_query (knowledge_graph.py:3798) and search() — both pure `LIKE '%q%'` over title/summary/metadata_json with keyword-hit re-ranking. SearchService.hybrid_search and vector_search (latticeai/services/search_service.py) exist and are exposed at /api/search/*, but no inference path calls them. The 'vector' memory tier is built, counted in the Memory Manager, rebuildable — and unused where it matters. Additionally the default embedder is feature-hashing ('lattice-local-hash-v1', latticeai/core/local_embeddings.py), which is lexical, not semantic; real providers (MLX/Ollama/OpenAI-compatible) exist in embedding_providers.py but are opt-in.

problems.title: Two disconnected knowledge stores injected into the same prompt (p_reinforce vault vs Knowledge Graph)
problems.detail: Every chat message triggers gardener.get_relevant_context (p_reinforce.py:130-148): an O(n) rglob over the entire ~/.ltcai-brain markdown vault, reading every file and substring-matching query keywords (any token len>1), returning the first 3 files' first 800 chars. This is a second, unindexed RAG path parallel to the KG, with rule-based classification (p_reinforce.py:54-70) and no linkage to KG provenance/ingestion (services/ingestion.py). It scales linearly with vault size on the chat hot path and its results carry no scores or trace entries.

problems.title: Recent-conversation context leaks other users' and other conversations' messages
problems.detail: build_recent_chat_context (latticeai/api/chat.py:163-187) filters with `item.get("user_email") == user_email or item.get("role") == "assistant"` — every assistant reply to ANY user passes the filter, and when conversation_id is absent the window spans all conversations. On a multi-user instance (org workspaces exist since v1.1.0) this injects other users' assistant responses into the model context. Mitigated only by the 50-message cap.

problems.title: Memory Manager reports placeholder health/size values and a hardcoded scope
problems.detail: memory_service.manager() hardcodes workspace_id="personal" for the workspace tier regardless of the caller's gated scope (memory_service.py:124), reports health:"ok" unconditionally for workspace/project/agent tiers (lines 147,152,157), and size_bytes:0 for project/agent/vector tiers. The 'unified façade' is real, but several displayed numbers are placeholders that the UI presents as live telemetry.

problems.title: Agent learning loop is lossy: markdown dump, swallowed errors, simulated snapshots
problems.detail: AgentRuntime.memory_update (latticeai/core/agent.py:417-439) extracts learnings via LLM and saves them as a markdown file in the vault's 30_Projects folder — not into workspace memories or the KG — and ends with bare `except Exception: pass`, so failures are invisible. Separately, the 'memory snapshots' produced by the multi_agent default_role_runner (latticeai/core/multi_agent.py:308-321) are deterministic canned dicts (researcher role = memory keyword search results), i.e. demo-grade orchestration artifacts, though workspace_os.create_memory_snapshot itself (UI path) snapshots real memories.

problems.title: workspace_os.json single-file store with silent retention caps
problems.detail: All memories, snapshots, traces, agent runs live in one JSON blob with full load_state/save_state rewrites per operation and silent truncation: memories[-500:] (workspace_os.py:1208), traces[-200:] (:905), memory_snapshots[-200:] (:1276). At Digital Brain scale this is both a durability risk (lost-update under concurrency, no WAL) and silent data loss contradicting 'knowledge is durable'.

problems.title: sessions.py is auth-only; there is no session/working-memory abstraction
problems.detail: latticeai/core/sessions.py is a token→email auth store (file-backed TTL map). Nothing in the system represents per-conversation working memory (active entities, open tasks, rolling summary). Doc-gen has an in-process _doc_gen_sessions dict (chat.py:159,426-430) that is lost on restart and never expires — the closest thing to working memory is an unbounded in-memory dict keyed by conversation_id.

strengths: Memory injection at inference time is real, not fake: latticeai/api/chat.py:365-418 demonstrably concatenates local vault knowledge, KG context (or multi-hop doc-gen context), OCR'd screenshots, auto-read file contents, and recent conversation into the prompt passed to router.generate/stream_generate.

Episodic record is durably written to the Knowledge Graph: every chat message becomes Message/AIResponse + Chat + Person nodes with extracted concepts and triples (knowledge_graph.py ingest_message:2597+), surviving the chat_history.json cap — the KG-first architecture has a genuine write side.

A provenance seed already exists end-to-end: build_graph_trace captures matched nodes/edges/source files per answer, record_trace persists it, and the trace_id + trace are streamed to the client in the SSE final frame (chat.py:461,632) — a solid foundation for v4's context-assembly-with-provenance.

The doc-gen context pipeline (latticeai/core/context_builder.py) does real hybrid scoring (0.5 text + 0.3 graph + 0.2 recency in search_for_document_generation) with 2-hop traversal, structured markdown sections, and source footnotes — the best-engineered retrieval path in the codebase, worth generalizing to all chat.

MemoryService is honest about availability (tiers report 'unavailable' rather than inventing counts), all mutating memory APIs are auth-gated and audited (latticeai/api/memory.py), and clear() requires explicit confirm.

Embedding infrastructure is properly abstracted: embedding_providers.py defines a provider interface with MLX/Ollama/OpenAI-compatible/custom options, index identity keyed by (model_id, dim) with stale/needs_reindex reporting, and explicit degradation reporting instead of silent faking.

Layering is clean and testable: router-factory pattern with injected ports (ChatService, MemoryService, AgentDeps), so a v4 context-assembly pipeline can be introduced behind existing seams without rewiring the app.
summary: Lattice AI today has six real, persisted memory surfaces (workspace memories in workspace_os.json, agent run snapshots, chat history, KG nodes/edges in SQLite, a vector index, and the p_reinforce markdown vault) unified behind a read-mostly MemoryService façade, and memory IS genuinely injected into model context at chat time — but injection is naive string concatenation of two disconnected keyword-search paths (vault substring scan + SQLite LIKE), while the purpose-built vector/hybrid search engine and the entire personal-memory tier (preferences/decisions/working_style) are never consumed at inference. Several displayed numbers are fabricated (hardcoded recall scores, synthesized trace confidence, placeholder health/size), the graph branch of /api/memory/recall is dead code due to a results/matches key bug masked by tests, and conversation memory is silently truncated to the last 50 messages globally. The strongest assets to build v4 on are the durable KG ingestion of every chat message, the per-answer trace/provenance plumbing already streamed to clients, and the doc-gen multi-hop context builder; the gap to a Digital Brain is the absence of automatic memory capture, episodic→semantic consolidation, experience/decision records, lifecycle management, and a budgeted context-assembly pipeline with full provenance.
